chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar that he had heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) narrate on the authority of his father (peace be upon him) that he had heard Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari say:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the sons of Abdul Mutalib, so he replied, 'Ten, and Abbas.'

The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: 'They were Abdullah, Abu Talib, Az-Zubayr, Hamzah, Harith who was the eldest, Qaydaq, Muqum, Hijl, Abd al-Aza who is Abu Lahab, Zarrar, and Abbas. And among the people is one who says that Muqum is Hijl. Abdul Mutalib had ten names by which the Arabs, the Roman Emperors, the Persian Kings, and the Ethiopian Kings knew him. Among his names were: Amir, Shaiba al-Hamd, Sayyid al-Batha, Saqi al-Hujjaj, Saqi al-Mughith, Ghayth al-Wara in the year of drought, Abu al-Sadat al-Ashara, Abdul Mutalib, Hafir Zamzam. And this was not for anyone who preceded him.'

key_terms.أبو لهب: Abu Lahab, uncle of the Prophet
key_terms.الغيداق: Qaydaq, one of the sons of Abdul Mutalib
key_terms.المقوم: Muqum, one of the sons of Abdul Mutalib
key_terms.حافر زمزم: Hafir Zamzam, one of Abdul Mutalib's names meaning 'digger of Zamzam'
key_terms.عبد المطلب: Abdul Mutalib, grandfather of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who were the ten sons of Abdul Mutalib and what were his unique names?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal establishes the lineage of the Prophet’s clan by listing the ten sons of Abdul Mutalib, specifically noting the scholarly variance on whether Muqum and Hijl are distinct or identical figures. It highlights Abdul Mutalib’s preeminent status through his ten unique epithets, such as 'Saqi al-Hujjaj' (Waterer of Pilgrims), which underscore his pivotal role in preparing the pilgrimage infrastructure for the Arab tribes before the advent of Islam.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-60 Ahmad ibn Zyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamedany - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar that he had heard Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB) narrate on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, “The Prophet (MGB) was asked about the number of the sons of Abdul Mutalib34 .

He (MGB) replied, ‘There were ten of them and Abbas.’” The compiler of the book - may God be pleased with him - said, “They were Abdullah; Abu Talib; Az-Zubayr; Hamzih; Harith who was the eldest; Qaydaq; Muqum; Hijl; Abd al-Aza who is the same as Abu Lahab36 ; Zarrar and Abbas. Some people say that Muqum is the same as Hijl. Abdul Mutalib had ten names by which the Arabs, the Roman Emperors and the Persian and Ethiopian Kings knew him. These names were: Amir; Shaiba-ulhamd; Sayyid Batha; Saqi Hujjaj; Saqi Muqays; Qays ul-vara fil-am ul-Judab; Abul Sadat ulashrat; Abdul Mutalib, Hafir Zamzam. Nobody had any of these names before him.”
